info.title: ToolboxPizza API
info.description:
Two modules.

BREAKS - self-service break tracking. A work day runs cutoff-to-cutoff UTC (06:00 by default) and a break belongs to the day it STARTED in, whole, even when it ends after the next cutoff. The daily limit is soft: breaks keep running past it and the overage is reported. The only actor is a User, who sets their own allowance and milestone thresholds.

TICKETS - internal ticketing keyed on a SECTION, a stable string the frontend tags each area with. Sections group under LEVELS, levels nest, and an assignment to a level covers every section beneath it. The load-bearing rule: a ticket only reaches someone who has the store, so a person assigned the section but lacking the store is not notified and gets 404 on its URL. Updates are POST, not PUT/PATCH. There are no bulk endpoints.

NOTE: GET /breaks/active and GET /breaks/day (current day only) evaluate milestones and can therefore WRITE rows. Do not prefetch, HEAD-probe or CDN-cache them.

NOTE: attachment bytes are served off the public disk with no bearer token - the one part of this API not covered by ext.authorized.

get.summary: Liveness, plus the user the token resolved to
The break picker, in display order
get.description: `group` is how a client blocks and headers the list; `counts_toward_limit` is the arithmetic. Read the boolean, never the group, when explaining a total.
Creates the settings row from the configured default on first read, so a client never needs a setup step.

post.summary: Replace the whole set of thresholds
post.description: Whole-list replacement, so the client never has to diff. Duplicates are collapsed and the list is sorted. An empty array turns milestones off. A threshold above the allowance is allowed - the limit is soft, so "tell me at 70" is meaningful against a 50-minute budget.

get.description: Also EVALUATES MILESTONES for the current work day - a client polling this to tick its timer is what notices a crossing. `belongs_to_previous_work_day` is true when the break started before the cutoff that has since passed.

200.description: The running break, or data: null

other_label.description: Required iff the chosen type has requires_custom_label; rejected otherwise.

200.description: A Laravel paginator of break entries

post.summary: Record a break the user forgot to time

post.description: POST, not PUT/PATCH - the house convention. Overwrites in place; there is no revision history. Send `ended_at: null` to reopen a break; omit the key to leave the end alone. Moving `started_at` across a cutoff recomputes `work_date`.

delete.summary: Delete a break and its notes

post.description: Allowed while the break is running and at any point afterwards, for as long as the entry is retained.

get.description: Defaults to the current work day. Evaluates milestones ONLY when the requested date is the current work day - a historical day is strictly read-only. A day with no breaks returns zeros, not a 404.

get.summary: The day breakdown plus a paste-ready text rendering
get.description: Same payload as /breaks/day plus `data.text`. A separate endpoint because /breaks/day is the polled one and should not render a document on every tick.

Everything the caller can see, across every store they can see it in.

THIS ROUTE HAS NO STORE IN THE PATH, so pizzasys makes no per-store decision on it (store_scope_mode = 'none'). ToolboxPizza filters it locally against the replicated user_store_roles - which is the whole reason that table is replicated. Three ways a ticket qualifies: the caller reported it, they are an explicit participant, or the section/level routing reaches them for that store.

parameters.name: statuses[]
parameters.description: OR within the filter. An unparseable value is dropped silently rather than 422'd.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Clamped, so a large value cannot pull the whole table.

parameters.name: stores[]
parameters.description: Store CODES. Narrows what the caller may already see; it can never widen it.

200.description: Paginated, most recently active first, id as the tiebreaker

post.description:
Raised against the store in the PATH; there is no store field in the body.

A ticket reaching nobody is NOT an error: it is created and the response carries data.warnings: ["no_recipients"], because refusing it would throw away someone's report over an admin's configuration gap.

Files are written to disk BEFORE the transaction opens and unlinked if it rolls back, so a failure can never strand bytes.

section_key.description: The routing key. Must be an ACTIVE section.

participants.description: The reporter MAY loop people in at creation; adding one later needs the manage-participants ability.

files.description: Attached to the ticket. Capped per request and checked against a sniffed mime allowlist.

notes.description: PAIRED BY INDEX: notes[0][files][] lands on the first note, never on the ticket.

201.description: The new ticket, presented for the caller

get.description:
Responses, notes, attachments and the whole status history.

404, never 403, when the caller has no relationship to it - a 403 would confirm the id exists. A ticket from another store is also 404 here, even for a caller who legitimately holds that other store.

post.description:
The reporter may edit only while the ticket is still `pending`: once somebody has picked it up, rewriting the description invalidates what they acted on. An assignee may edit at any status.

section_key RE-ROUTES the ticket to a different audience, so it needs the change-status ability rather than the edit one.

Assignees only - the reporter follows and replies but does not decide when their own problem is solved.

An illegal transition is 409 TICKET_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION carrying `allowed`, and writes no audit row. Moving to the status it is already in is 409 too, rather than an audit row saying nothing happened.

200.description: The audit row that was written

post.summary: Reopen a fixed or closed ticket
post.description: The one edge back out of a terminal state. A REASON IS REQUIRED - reopening says the previous answer was wrong, and the person who gave it needs to know why. Clears fixed_at/closed_at, bumps reopen_count, and the audit row carries is_reopen = true.
Readers cannot: that is the difference between a reader and a responder. The first reply stamps first_responded_at once and never again.
Same authority as replying - a note remarks on the ticket rather than changing it.
Capped per request, and checked against a SNIFFED mime allowlist - text/html and image/svg+xml are excluded on purpose, because both execute script on a publicly-served origin.

Assignees only: routing belongs to the people who own the queue, not to the reporter.

Re-adding someone CHANGES THEIR ROLE rather than stacking a second grant. Adding the reporter is 422 TICKET_PARTICIPANT_REDUNDANT - they already read and reply by virtue of reporting, and a row saying so would be a second source of truth.

role=assignee is the escape hatch: full powers on this one ticket though the section is not theirs.

delete.description: Only removes an explicit row. Somebody the section routing reaches stays reachable - take the assignment away for that.

get.summary: Who this ticket reaches, and why
get.description: The resolution made observable. `user_ids` is who would actually be notified (section/level routing INTERSECTED with store access); `candidates` is everyone the routing reaches before the store filter, each with `via` naming the section or the level they came through. The difference between the two lists is exactly the people the store rule excluded.

200.description: Resolved recipients and the candidates behind them

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description: Off by default, so the picker only ever sees live rows.

post.description: The `key` is what the frontend hardcodes, so it is chosen once and never renamed. Display names are free to change.

delete.description: DEACTIVATES it. Tickets point at these rows forever, so nothing is ever actually deleted.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description: Off by default, so the picker only ever sees live rows.

get.description: Always nested - a flat list of levels tells you nothing, since what a level covers is defined by what sits under it.

post.description: Re-parenting is checked against the graph: a parent that is the node itself or any of its descendants is 422 TICKET_LEVEL_CYCLE, carrying the offending `path`.

delete.description: Deactivates it, and hands back assignments_affected: HOW MANY PEOPLE STOP RECEIVING. An inactive level severs the chain above it, so deactivating a mid-tree level silently cuts off everyone assigned higher up - this count is there so that is a decision rather than a surprise.

200.description: The now-inactive level and the blast radius

post.summary: Set which sections sit under a level
post.description: WHOLE-LIST REPLACE, mirroring break-milestones: [] detaches everything. A section may sit under several levels at once.

post.summary: Assign someone to a section or a level
post.description:
EXACTLY ONE of ticket_section_id / ticket_level_id. Neither is 422 TICKET_ASSIGNMENT_TARGET_REQUIRED; both is TICKET_ASSIGNMENT_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS.

store_scoped is the whole store story: true means 'this section, at the stores they hold', false means 'this section, everywhere'. Stores are never named here.

delete.description: A REAL delete, unlike sections and levels: an assignment is configuration, not history.

bearerAuth.description: A pizzasys user token. Verified on every request; there is no local login. An employee-subject token is refused outright - employees are a different id space.

date.name: date
date.description: A WORK date. Defaults to the current work day.

storeId.name: storeId
storeId.description: The store CODE, not the numeric pk. 404 STORE_NOT_FOUND if it has not replicated here yet.

requires_custom_label.description: True only for "Custom / Other", which needs other_label on the entry.

label.description: other_label when present, else the type name - so clients never branch on the catalog-or-free-text split.

ended_at.description: null means the break is running.

duration_minutes.description: Floored. Entry minutes need not sum to the day total.

counts_toward_limit.description: A snapshot taken at write time, not a live catalog join.

source.description: Entry ORIGIN, not an edit trail.

self_reported.description: Always true. Breaks are editable in place with no revision history, so this document is what the user says happened - not evidence.

Attachment.description: Served straight off the public disk via the storage:link symlink. The URL needs no token - anyone holding it reads the file.

TicketParticipant.description: Somebody added to one ticket by hand, independently of the section routing.

TicketStatusChange.description: One row per transition, including the ticket's own creation (from_status null).

allowed_transitions.description: What the server would honour from here. Render these as buttons instead of discovering a 409.

warnings.description: On creation only. ["no_recipients"] means the ticket was stored but the section reaches nobody who has this store.

viewer.description: THE CALLER'S OWN capabilities. Absent from broadcast payloads, which are viewer-neutral because one envelope reaches many people.

TicketSection.description: Retired via `active`, never deleted - tickets point at these rows forever.

TicketLevel.description: Levels nest. Deactivating one SEVERS the chain above it: a section under an inactive level stops reaching everyone higher up.

TicketAssignment.description: Exactly one of section/level. Stores are never named here - store_scoped decides whether the person's own store grants filter what reaches them.

store_scoped.description: true = only tickets for stores this user holds. false = every store. A user matching several rows is unscoped if ANY of them is.

Settings.description: Allowance, thresholds and the work-day config

Unauthorized.description: No token, an inactive token, or a user that has not replicated yet

Forbidden.description: pizzasys returned ext.authorized=false, or the token is not a user subject

NotFound.description: No such break for this user. 404 rather than 403, so ids cannot be probed.

DomainConflict.description: A domain rule refused the change. `error.code` is the contract: ALREADY_ON_BREAK, BREAK_OVERLAP (carries error.conflicts), BREAK_NOT_RUNNING, BREAK_ENDS_BEFORE_START, BREAK_STARTS_IN_FUTURE, BREAK_OUTSIDE_RETENTION_WINDOW, BREAK_CUSTOM_LABEL_REQUIRED, BREAK_CUSTOM_LABEL_NOT_ALLOWED, BREAK_TYPE_INACTIVE.
